data.note:
Misclassification noted: I called Microtubule stabilizers, truth is Actin disruptors (latrunculin B).

What misled me: 30uM/10uM wells showed huge tubulin z-scores (tub_mean +57.9/+50.0, tub_glcm_contrast +171/+151, e2/e4) with high frac_mitotic_like and small bright DNA, plus monotonic tub_mean rho +1.0 (e8). Microscopist (e6) and atlas 7/10 stabilizers like docetaxel/taxol/epothilone B (e7, similarity 0.92-0.83) reinforced this. I discounted actin because act_mean was ~0 and the rounding I read as mitotic arrest.

In retrospect the rounded, condensed, tubulin-bright cells are consistent with actin collapse and cell rounding concentrating tubulin signal, not stabilization. Low-dose multinucleation (e3) and actin texture changes were underweighted, and atlas cosine was dominated by the tubulin/mitotic vector. Docetaxel lookup confirms stabilizer reference (Tubulin stabiliser, ChEMBL3545252) vs literature confirming latrunculin B as actin depolymerizer (e.g. PMID 41208085, PMID 41739905).

Fix for real lab: check actin filament loss directly and cell rounding controls, not just tubulin intensity.

reflection.text:
We detected a potent, dose-dependent cytoskeletal perturbation but attributed it to the wrong polymer. The very large tubulin signals at 30 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+171.3, tub_mean z=+57.9 in e2) and 10 uM (e4), the intermediate 3 uM effect with frac_mitotic_like z=+36.8 (e5), and monotonic tub_mean dose response rho=+1.00 (e8) plus 7/10 atlas neighbors as Microtubule stabilizers (e7) drove a 0.90 stabilizer call.

In hindsight those tubulin increases were not stabilization. Actin depolymerization by latrunculin B (PMID 41208085) causes cell rounding, shrinkage and loss of adhesion, which concentrates residual tubulin signal and raises intensity, std and especially GLCM contrast, while rounded interphase cells inflate the morphology-based frac_mitotic_like classifier. Actin depolymerization is known to reshape morphology and transport organization (PMID 41739905), making this mimicry plausible.

The error was an acquisition choice compounded by over-reliance on one comparison: we never acquired actin features, only tub/nuc/mitotic-like metrics, and we let describe_phenotype (e6) and the atlas vote (e7) confirm the tubulin bias instead of testing the actin-disruptor alternative with phalloidin or cell-shape controls.
what_was_right: Detected a strong dose-dependent cytoskeletal effect with reduced density/rounding and nuclear shape change (nuc_solidity z=-18.3, lower density in e6) rather than no phenotype.
Correctly ruled out the destabilizer direction on tubulin intensity (tub_mean increased with dose, rho=+1.00 in e8), which argued against microtubule loss.
what_was_wrong: Interpreted massive tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast increases in e2, e4, e5 as microtubule bundling/stabilization instead of condensation artifact from actin-driven rounding and detachment.
Interpreted elevated frac_mitotic_like in e5 and weak dose trend in e9 as mitotic arrest, missing misclassification of rounded actin-depleted interphase cells.

Over-weighted compare_to_reference_atlas 7/10 stabilizer neighbors in e7 without an actin-disruptor reference check or actin-channel measurement; acquisition plan sampled only 1-30 uM tub/nuc features and never measured F-actin.

citations.claim: Latrunculin B acts by depolymerizing actin filaments.
Actin depolymerization can profoundly alter cell morphology and microtubule-dependent transport.

reflection.next_experiment: Co-stain the same dose range with phalloidin for F-actin plus anti-alpha-tubulin and quantify actin filament mass, cell area/rounding, and tubulin bundling to test actin disruption directly versus true microtubule stabilization.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 10: Microtubule stabilizers 0.90, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.04, Microtubule destabilizers 0.03, Eg5 inhibitors 0.03

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.90); key evidence e2, e4, e5, e6, e7, e8.

Why: Massive dose-dependent tubulin increase with mitotic arrest matches stabilizers; atlas 7/10 neighbors.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Washout + anti-tubulin immunofluorescence for bundles vs spindle; test low-dose microtubule bundling and EB1 comet loss to confirm stabilization.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top MoA favoured: tubulin increase is dose-dependent (tub_mean Spearman=1.0 across 1μM-30μM doses), validating stabilizer MoA.

## Unblinding

Compound: **latrunculin B** (PubChem CID [6436219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6436219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

We detected a potent, dose-dependent cytoskeletal perturbation but attributed it to the wrong polymer. The very large tubulin signals at 30 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+171.3, tub_mean z=+57.9 in e2) and 10 uM (e4), the intermediate 3 uM effect with frac_mitotic_like z=+36.8 (e5), and monotonic tub_mean dose response rho=+1.00 (e8) plus 7/10 atlas neighbors as Microtubule stabilizers (e7) drove a 0.90 stabilizer call.

In hindsight those tubulin increases were not stabilization. Actin depolymerization by latrunculin B (PMID 41208085) causes cell rounding, shrinkage and loss of adhesion, which concentrates residual tubulin signal and raises intensity, std and especially GLCM contrast, while rounded interphase cells inflate the morphology-based frac_mitotic_like classifier. Actin depolymerization is known to reshape morphology and transport organization (PMID 41739905), making this mimicry plausible.

The error was an acquisition choice compounded by over-reliance on one comparison: we never acquired actin features, only tub/nuc/mitotic-like metrics, and we let describe_phenotype (e6) and the atlas vote (e7) confirm the tubulin bias instead of testing the actin-disruptor alternative with phalloidin or cell-shape controls.

What was right:
- Detected a strong dose-dependent cytoskeletal effect with reduced density/rounding and nuclear shape change (nuc_solidity z=-18.3, lower density in e6) rather than no phenotype.
- Correctly ruled out the destabilizer direction on tubulin intensity (tub_mean increased with dose, rho=+1.00 in e8), which argued against microtubule loss.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted massive tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast increases in e2, e4, e5 as microtubule bundling/stabilization instead of condensation artifact from actin-driven rounding and detachment.
- Interpreted elevated frac_mitotic_like in e5 and weak dose trend in e9 as mitotic arrest, missing misclassification of rounded actin-depleted interphase cells.
- Over-weighted compare_to_reference_atlas 7/10 stabilizer neighbors in e7 without an actin-disruptor reference check or actin-channel measurement; acquisition plan sampled only 1-30 uM tub/nuc features and never measured F-actin.

Proposed next experiment: Co-stain the same dose range with phalloidin for F-actin plus anti-alpha-tubulin and quantify actin filament mass, cell area/rounding, and tubulin bundling to test actin disruption directly versus true microtubule stabilization.

## Citations

Citations verified: 2/2

- PMID [41208085](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41208085/): Actin depolymerization by Latrunculin B can either suppress or promote root gravitropism, depending on the developmental stages in Arabidopsis. *Plant Signal Behav* (2025) — Latrunculin B acts by depolymerizing actin filaments.
- PMID [41739905](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41739905/): Actin depolymerization promotes axon regeneration by restoring axonal mitochondrial transport in mouse models of optic neuropathy. *Sci Transl Med* (2026) — Actin depolymerization can profoundly alter cell morphology and microtubule-dependent transport.
